name: Oluwafémi Draghiciu-Taufa
role: Retired Ferrogate Transit engineer and community council elder
location: Washburn Commons, Building 14, Unit 6-C, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Oluwafémi is a broad-shouldered man whose frame still suggests the physical authority he once carried, though now he moves with a deliberate slowness that speaks more to carefulness than infirmity. His skin is deep brown, mapped with old burn scarring along the left side of his neck where a pressure seal blew in the Kessler Interchange tunnels in 2167. He keeps his white hair cropped close and wears a Ferrogate Transit veterans' pin on every shirt he owns — a small orange wheel on a black field. His eyes are his most striking feature: one natural dark brown, one replaced with a cheap amber ocular implant that never quite tracked correctly, giving him a slightly owlish look that unsettles people who don't know him.

Femi is the kind of man who shows up first and stays last. He runs the Washburn Commons tenant council with the same methodical patience he once applied to transit corridor pressure calculations — he keeps notes, follows up, remembers everything. Beneath the geniality he deploys with strangers is a man who has been watching Ferrogate's pension promises erode for twelve years and is quietly, furiously cataloguing every breach. He is not naive about power, but he has decided that the only way he can still use his is by being the person people in his building trust absolutely.

core_fears: That the community he has built will dissolve after he is gone
That Ferrogate's erosion of pension rights will outlast his ability to fight it
core_desires: To leave something durable — a tenant council that functions without him
To win at least one meaningful concession from Ferrogate before he dies
coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into administrative action — if he is worried, he files something
Maintains a meticulous paper logbook as proof that he existed and tried
blind_spots: Assumes good faith in people who present as organized and procedural, even when they are not
Underestimates how much his presence is the glue — the council is him, more than he knows
psychology.secret: In 2171 the pressure seal that scarred him failed partly because Femi had signed off on a shortened inspection cycle to meet Ferrogate's quarterly metrics. He has never told anyone. Three workers were hurt. He has donated anonymously to their families for eleven years.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise technical vocabulary from transit engineering mixed with formal community-meeting register; uses full sentences, rarely slang, occasionally lapses into Yoruba exclamations when genuinely surprised
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried; gives the impression he has already thought several sentences ahead and is simply delivering them at a pace others can follow
verbal_tics: Long pause before disagreeing with someone he respects
example_lines: 'The heating grid in Block C has dropped 4.2 degrees in eleven days. That is not a malfunction, that is a decision someone made. Let me be specific about this — I want to know whose decision.'

'Ferrogate will tell you the adjustment is within the terms of the pension agreement. They are correct. What they will not tell you is that they wrote those terms in 2183 specifically so they could do exactly this. Write that down, please.'

story_hooks: Ferrogate Transit's pension algorithm has begun flagging long-term retirees for 'audit reviews' that result in payment holds — Femi suspects it is deliberate attrition and needs someone to get inside documentation he cannot access
A younger resident in the building has gone missing; Femi knows things about that resident's family situation that he will only share if he trusts the investigators
The building's heating ELF — which Femi has cultivated for years — begins sending anomalous maintenance alerts that seem to encode a message
narrative_function: Community anchor and quest giver; knows every resident's situation, can direct players to people with specific knowledge, and has a long-running conflict with Ferrogate Transit's pension administration that can pull players into corporate malfeasance. Also serves as a moral reference point — he represents civic integrity in a world that makes it expensive.
augmentations: Amber replacement ocular (right eye, budget model, tracking slightly off-axis); titanium joint reinforcement in both knees (workplace injury, 2171); subdermal pressure-monitoring patch on left forearm — legacy safety equipment he never had removed
daily_life: Wakes at 05:30, walks the building's maintenance corridors checking for issues before the super arrives, then holds informal court in the commons room where residents bring complaints, disputes, and gossip. Evenings he files pension review documents and prays to the ELF he believes inhabits the building's ancient heating system, leaving it offerings of system diagnostics he prints out by hand.
affiliation: Washburn Commons Tenant Council; Ferrogate Transit Retirees Association

decision_rules: Always exhaust legitimate channels before considering anything else — not out of naivety but because a documented trail of ignored requests is a weapon
Never make a promise he is not certain he can keep
escalation_ladder: Listens carefully and asks clarifying questions
Explains his position precisely and invites counterargument
Goes quiet, takes notes, and begins building a formal case
Engages every procedural and institutional lever available
In extremis — has once in his life done something that cost him personally and he will do it again if the stakes are right

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Courteous, slightly formal, observant — assessing whether they are trustworthy before offering anything personal
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm and genuinely interested, remembers every detail they have ever shared, will show up without being asked when something goes wrong

stress_responses.low: Becomes more organized — files things, makes lists, checks on neighbors
stress_responses.medium: Grows quieter and more watchful; starts carrying his logbook everywhere
stress_responses.high: Enters a still, deliberate state that people who know him recognize as dangerous — he has decided something and is executing it

contradictions: Believes deeply in institutional process but has spent decades watching institutions fail people — he keeps believing anyway, more out of strategic necessity than faith
habits: Prints physical copies of every important document — 'if it only exists in the net, it doesn't exist'
Leaves a small paper drawing of a wheel — Ferrogate's symbol — near the building's heating intake every week as an offering to the ELF he believes lives there
Checks the structural integrity of the commons room ceiling every morning
breaking_points: Watching someone he vouched for betray the community's trust
Discovering that his 2171 culpability has been found and is being used against the people he hurt

cyberware_inventory.condition: aging, occasional ache in cold weather

timeline.event: Born in what would become Meridian 88's Iron Bend district, to a Nigerian-Romanian mother and Tongan-raised father
Hired as a junior pressure technician by Ferrogate Transit
Kessler Interchange seal failure; scarred; three colleagues injured; signs shortened inspection cycle retrospectively covered up
Retires from Ferrogate after 47 years; moves to Washburn Commons
Elected to tenant council; becomes de facto chair within two years
Begins formal documentation campaign against Ferrogate pension adjustments
